public_rationale: The speaker said autonomy needs consistency, reliability and replicability, and that LLMs lacked them. Independent evaluations from the year before the post agree. On tau-bench, a frontier model (GPT-4o) succeeded on under half of tasks, and on under a quarter of retail tasks when it had to succeed in all 8 tries. METR found in March 2025 that the best model reached 80% reliability only on tasks of about 15 minutes, and concluded that models cannot reliably perform moderate-length tasks. The counterpoint is that models did finish bounded tasks alone some of the time, and that ability was growing quickly. Under his own definition, though, partial and inconsistent success is not autonomy. So the claim holds for the period it describes.
limitations: The grade depends on using the speaker's own definition of autonomy; a looser definition (any task done without a human) would weaken support.
The tau-bench result is from mid-2024; newer models in early 2025 scored higher on single attempts.

our_interpretation: The speaker defines autonomy in the same sentence: it needs consistency, reliability and replicability. The test uses his definition: at the time of the post, could LLM systems do work on their own, and do it dependably and repeatably?

Finishing some bounded tasks some of the time (for example at 50% success) is not autonomy under his definition. Evidence of high, repeatable success on realistic multi-step work with no human help would count against him.
He names no period. I read this as the state of frontier LLM systems in the year before the post (2024-06-01 to the post date, 2025-06-09).
criteria.support_condition: Independent evaluations from the period show frontier LLM agents failing much realistic multi-step work, succeeding inconsistently across repeated attempts, or unable to stay highly reliable on tasks of moderate length.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent evaluations from the period show LLM agents finishing realistic multi-step tasks with no human help at high and repeatable success rates, which would show the consistency and reliability he says they lack.
